newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks hammered by inflation worries.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks hammered by inflation worries.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average fell nearly 150 points Friday on signs that underlying inflation was showing some unwanted vitality and as long-term interest rates soared to the highest levels since last July.

Based on early and unofficial data, the Dow finished with a loss of 148.36 points, or 2.27 percent, at 6,391.69. It was off 134.38 points for the week, its fifth straight down week. The last time the index racked up such a string of declining weeks was in the last quarter of 1991.
In the broader market, declining issues swamped advances 23-3 on active volume of 442 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
